title: Self-assembly of luminescent 42-metal lanthanide nanowheels with sensing properties towards metal ions and nitro explosives

synthesis.procedure: Yb acetate and HL were dissolved in ethanol at room temperature. Triethylamine solution in ethanol was added, and the mixture was stirred under reflux for 30 min. After cooling and filtration, diethyl ether was slowly diffused into the filtrate at room temperature. Pale yellow crystals formed after one week; they were filtered, washed with ethanol and dried in air for one week.

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.amount: 1 mL of a 1.0 mol L−1 solution in ethanol

synthesis.temperature: Room temperature initially and during crystallization; reflux during reaction
synthesis.time: 30 min reflux; one week crystallization; one week drying
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Stirred reflux followed by diethyl ether diffusion into the filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled and filtered; pale yellow crystals obtained by slow diethyl ether diffusion, filtered, washed with ethanol (3 × 5 mL), and dried in air.

properties.summary: Displays Yb(III) near-infrared emission upon ligand excitation. Its emission in acetonitrile responds to metal ions and nitro explosives, notably quenching by Cu(II) and 2-nitrophenol and enhancement by Cd(II).

source_locations.location: Luminescence properties, Table 1; Luminescent sensing to analytes

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A discrete 42-Yb wheel-like nanocluster approximately 3.6 nm in external diameter, 1.5 nm in internal diameter and 1.1 nm thick. Intermolecular contacts pack the wheels into an open three-dimensional channel structure in the solid state.
